title: System design, from the ground up
subtitle: Build a strong foundation. Understand real platforms. Practice interviews with confidence.
description: Start with the building blocks, explained patiently with worked examples. The first eight weeks contain 36 foundation chapters before larger design problems. Then connect distributed systems, reliability, Kubernetes, MCP, and AI infrastructure with interview practice. Core teaching stays on your laptop; external resources are optional.
pace: 24 flexible weeks. Weeks contain five to nine study steps. Spread them across the week or combine them into longer sessions every two days. Some foundation weeks include an extra visual workshop. Repeat a week when the ideas are still unclear; the calendar is a guide, not a deadline.
readiness: Use your recorded explanations and mock feedback to find remaining gaps. Reading a chapter is progress; readiness comes from applying it to unfamiliar problems and explaining your tradeoffs.

stages.title: 1. Understand the building blocks
stages.description: A broad foundation in computers, requests, APIs, protocols, memory, SQL, data models, and storage. New terms are explained from scratch.

stages.title: 2. Understand the working components
stages.description: Learn proxies, services, Redis, cache patterns, containers, and queues in depth before combining them.

stages.title: 3. Make several machines work together
stages.description: Reason about copies, partitions, retries, and permissions through concrete timelines.

stages.title: 4. Operate and explain your designs
stages.description: Understand reliability and Kubernetes operations, then begin structured interview practice.

stages.title: 5. Design complete products
stages.description: Work through chat, feeds, file storage, video, and search with evolving requirements.

stages.title: 6. Handle difficult tradeoffs and mocks
stages.description: Study coordination, MCP platforms, GPU serving, and difficult tradeoffs before final mocks.
